title: Chapter 4
content:
Priceless porcelain and museum-grade paintings lined the corridors beside antique wooden furniture. Vases bursting with lush, fragrant blooms were artfully arranged throughout the estate, while house staff bustled past, navigating heavy serving carts laden with food.

In the center of it all stood a middle-aged man in a tailored suit, directing the staff with quiet precision. This was Butler Yang, the man who ran the main estate with an iron fist. As he instructed a maid to swap out a spotted fork, footsteps approached behind him. Adjusting his glasses, Butler Yang turned to find the family's second son: Kang Il-hyun.

"Ah, Executive Director Kang. You’ve arrived."

"Good to see you again, Butler Yang."

"The Chairman and Madam Kim will be joining us downstairs in thirty minutes."

"Understood. I'll wait."

With a polite smile and a deep bow, Butler Yang returned to his duties. Watching the old man's crisp, measured movements as he gave instructions to the staff, Il-hyun slipped into thought.

How old was I when I first met him? It had been so long he could barely remember. He must have been a boy—well over two decades ago, back when his birth mother was still alive. Even then, Butler Yang never let his mask slip. Whether Il-hyun’s mother was screaming at him or slapping his face in a fit of rage, the man had worn that exact same mild, pleasant smile.

The harsh scraping of a chair pulled Il-hyun back to the present.

Kang Yu-jung dropped into the seat beside him. Dressed in a simple tee and worn jeans, she practically radiated exhaustion. Unlike her three brothers, who were all entrenched in the family’s corporate empire, Yu-jung was a surgeon. She spent her days knee-deep in blood and gore, but claimed to love every minute of it.

"I didn't think you'd make it," Il-hyun said.

"I came to see you, little brother," she purred, reaching out with an exaggerated pout. "It's been way too long. Come here, give your big sister a hug."

Il-hyun cringed, leaning his torso as far back as the chair would allow. Seeing his perpetually stoic face contort in genuine revulsion, Yu-jung burst into a bright laugh.

"Having fun?" he asked dryly.

"Look in a mirror! You look hilarious. If you could see your own decaying expression right now, you'd understand."

"What a bizarre hobby."

"Don't be so cold," she teased. "Have you forgotten we're on the same team?"

Il-hyun let out a dry snort. Team.

Yu-jung was the only sibling who shared the same mother with him. But like Il-hyun, she carried no fond memories of the woman who bore them. Right up until the moment she hanged herself from the second-floor balcony—strung out on booze and pills—their mother had never offered them a single drop of affection. Not that it was entirely her fault; forced into an unwanted political marriage, she had no love left to spare for the children spawned from it.

"Look who’s early," a voice called out.

Kang Tae-han and his wife, Park Sun-joo, arrived to join the table. Gone was the modest, unassuming woman who had dished out soup to the homeless yesterday; Sun-joo was now decked out in heavy makeup and a glamorous designer dress. She greeted Yu-jung with particular enthusiasm. Despite being sisters-in-law, the two got along famously, bound by shared tastes and unexpectedly candid personalities.

"The Chairman and Madam Kim are descending," Butler Yang announced.

As if on cue, all four siblings stood up in unison.

Chairman Kang descended the sweeping spiral staircase leaning heavily on a cane, supported on his right by Kim Sun-young—his third wife and Seok-joo’s mother. Though the old man walked fine on his own, Sun-young fussed over him with suffocating devotion. Trailing a few paces behind them was Kang Seok-joo, his temple still bandaged from where Il-hyun had driven an ice pick into his skull the previous night.

Chairman Kang took his place at the head of the table, flanked by Sun-young and Seok-joo.

"Sit, everyone," the Chairman grunted.

The moment they sat, Kim Sun-young’s icy glare locked straight onto Kang Il-hyun. Even as the staff began taking their entree orders, her gaze never wavered.

Il-hyun set his water glass down, addressing her point-blank. "Is there something on your mind, Mother?"

His tone was sweet, but the air in the dining hall instantly turned arctic. Il-hyun knew better than anyone that Sun-young wouldn't let the attack on her precious golden boy slide without a fight.

"Shouldn't you be offering an apology before I even have to ask?" she snapped, her voice trembling with suppressed rage. "You put a hole in your own brother's head!"

Il-hyun drifted his eyes away from Sun-young, letting them land on Seok-joo. A white gauze patch was taped over his temple. The moment their eyes met, Seok-joo cowered like prey cornered by a predator, dropping his gaze instantly.

Sun-young’s face contorted in disgust as she rounded on her son. "Lift your head up! Are you an idiot? What are you bowing your head for?!"

"Why don't we ask the boy himself?" Il-hyun interjected smoothly, leaning forward. "Well, Seok-joo? Tell us. Did I do something that warrants an apology?"

"..."

"Answer me. If you want an apology, I'll give you one right here in front of everyone."

Seok-joo’s eyes darted frantically around the table. High on drugs, he was a brave tyrant, but sitting here sober was absolute torture. The cold, piercing gazes of his siblings felt like knives digging into his skin.

"N-No... it's fine, Brother," Seok-joo stammered, his voice barely a whisper. "It was... it was my fault. You don't need to apologize..."

Il-hyun let out a dramatic, sorrowful sigh, turning back to Sun-young with a pitying smile. "You heard him, Mother. My little brother says I did nothing wrong."

"You arrogant little—"

"Enough!" Chairman Kang barked, slamming a fist on the armrest. "Not at the dinner table!"

Silence descended instantly. Kim Sun-young bit her lower lip, casting a resentful glance at her husband. She knew the Chairman blatantly favored Il-hyun—partly because the boy was frighteningly capable, and partly because he was the spitting image of his father in his youth. Still, watching her husband turn a blind eye to Il-hyun's brutality made her blood boil. Beneath the tablecloth, her hands squeezed into tight fists.

Once the main course was served, the suffocating tension gradually eased into polite corporate chatter. They discussed business matters, interspersed with light updates about Tae-han’s twins and Yu-jung’s hospital.

"When did Chang say his boy was arriving?" the Chairman asked between sips of red wine.

Tae-han answered first. "Tomorrow, sir."

"Where is he staying?"

Il-hyun paused mid-slice, raising the tip of his steak knife slightly. "I'll be hosting him at my residence."

"Take good care of him," the Chairman instructed. "Chang's boy is as good as family to you boys."

At the word family, Il-hyun offered a faint, almost invisible smirk. Right. As if I don't have enough fucking brothers already.

"Of course, Father. I'll see to it personally."

Just then, Il-hyun’s eyes caught Seok-joo, who flinched every time their gazes crossed. Watching his half-brother squirm was entertaining, but a much better idea suddenly popped into Il-hyun's head.

"Actually... come to think of it, Seok-joo might be a better host. They're the exact same age, so I'm sure they'll hit it off instantly."

Seok-joo’s knife slipped, screeching loudly against his porcelain plate. His head snapped up in sheer horror. Why was the target suddenly painted on his back?

Across the table, Il-hyun raised his wine glass, flashing him a radiant, villainous smile.

A cold shudder ran down Seok-joo’s spine. He immediately averted his eyes, clutching his cutlery tightly under the table. He had no idea what sick game Il-hyun was playing, but deep in his chest, he made a silent, burning vow: One of these days, I'm going to kill that bastard with my own two hands.

"I have always harbored a deep passion for traditional Korean art, which is why I asked my grandfather for permission to visit."

Watching Jakyeong recite the line like a malfunctioning android, Wang Han clicked his tongue. Jesus. A modern AI could pull off more emotion than that.

To infiltrate Kang Il-hyun’s house, Jakyeong had to pose as someone else—and his cover identity happened to be a frail, pampered young master. Wang Han gave Jakyeong a slow, doubtful once-over from head to toe.

Jakyeong’s skin was deeply bronzed from the scorching Thai sun, and even behind a pair of blue-light glasses, his eyes burned with a terrifying, predatory sharp intensity. To top it off, he had a massive, gaping snake tattooed right across his shoulder. Who in their right mind is going to look at this lethal killer and see a delicate rich kid?

"Jakyeong, you are not stepping one foot outside until we fly out," Wang Han sighed. "We need to pray that tan fades."

"My skin?"

"You used to be pale as a sheet when you were younger! Even two years ago in Shanghai, you didn't look like a hardened mercenary. If you lock yourself in the house for two weeks, maybe you'll look slightly less lethal."

Jakyeong pursed his lips, his chin wrinkling as he fell into deep thought.

To pull off this hit, he had to impersonate a man named Jang Yi-an. Yi-an was the grandson of a powerful Triad boss in Hong Kong—a greenhouse flower who had lost his father at a young age and was raised in pure luxury by his Korean mother and wealthy grandfather.

Jakyeong, on the other hand, was a wild weed. A persistent, indestructible weed that survived no matter how many times it was stomped into the dirt. They were both green, sure, but they weren't even in the same species.

"Who do you think put out the contract?" Jakyeong asked suddenly, curiosity breaking his train of thought.

Wang Han had been running the numbers. "My money's on someone within Haewon Group. It takes a heavy hitter to use Dmitri as a middleman for an assassination of this scale. Someone with enough pull to swap out the grandson of an underworld kingpin... and enough collateral to ensure they don't get caught."

"So, family."

It was a story as old as time in their line of work. Family stabbing family, friends putting hits on friends. Lovers were no exception either—plenty of people had no qualms about putting a bullet through the head of the person they’d shared a bed with the night before. It was precisely why Jakyeong never trusted anyone, and why he kept the world at arm's length.

"Well, whoever hired me," Jakyeong said, a smirk spreading across his face, "they're going to realize hiring me was the best decision of their life."

Wang Han shook his head at Jakyeong’s boundless bravado. "With your acting skills? You're going to get exposed in five minutes."

"Am I really that bad?"

Wang Han stared hard at Jakyeong's face. His eyes were large and strikingly defined, bordered by subtle double eyelids. But depending on where he looked, his impression shifted dramatically. The skin around his eyelids had a natural reddish hue—when he looked down, he appeared strangely tragic and vulnerable; but when he looked up, the corners of his eyes tilted into something dangerous and sharp. Women usually went crazy for it.

"Mmm... try softening your eyes," Wang Han instructed. "Right now, you look like you're about to murder everyone in the room."

Taking the advice literally, Jakyeong blinked rapidly, opening his eyes wide and fluttering them to loosen his facial muscles. "Like this?"

Wang Han winced. Now he just looked completely brain-dead. Watching Jakyeong's brown pupils wander aimlessly under his drooping eyelids, Wang Han shook his head. "Forget it. Stop."

"How about this then?" Jakyeong crossed his eyes intentionally, pulling a ridiculous face.

Wang Han groaned. "If you're going to waste a face like that, hand it over to me." He paused, his expression turning serious. "Look, fine, we'll figure out the face. But whatever you do, do not get caught naked. If anyone sees those combat scars covering your torso, the cover is blown instantly."

Jakyeong cracked a dry laugh and leaned back into his chair.

"Relax. Why would I be taking my clothes off? It's not like I'm going to seduce Kang Il-hyun."

Translator's Notes (A/N):

Executive Director (상무): In Korean corporate hierarchy, Sang-mu (상무) is a high-ranking executive position, roughly equivalent to a Managing Director or Vice President.
Haewon Group (해운그룹): The overarching corporate conglomerate owned and operated by the Kang family as a legitimate front for their syndicate activities.
"Triad" / "Black Societies" (흑사회): Heuk-sa-hoe* (흑사회) is the Korean term used to refer to Chinese organized crime syndicates or Triads.
